warnings.why: Equatorial Guinea relies heavily on oil and gas revenues and corporate taxes from hydrocarbons, but its non-oil tax revenue collection is generally weak, making a reported 79.2% share of income taxes out of total taxes implausibly high compared to standard macroeconomic profiles.

Angola derives a vast majority of its government revenue from petroleum production and associated royalties rather than broad-based personal or corporate income taxes, making a 70.1% share from income, profits, and capital gains inconsistent with its known tax structure.

policy: model memory is advisory; unsupported suspicions cannot overrule official data
